The *Raṁsisaññakattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. Classified within the later strata of the Sutta Piṭaka, the text recounts the past deeds and aspirations of the elder (thera) Raṁsisaññaka [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text across five modern languages, although it does not provide an English title [SuttaCentral].
No cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are reported by SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus identifies automated text-reuse patterns involving ten shared passages across four other poems in the *Therāpadāna* [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual correspondence is with its companion text, the *Dutiyaraṁsisaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 88), featuring four matching segments with a near-identical core sequence (§4.2–7.1 aligned with Tha-Ap 88 §3.2–6.1 at 0.96 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. Additional formulaic passages are shared with the *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 270), the *Tiṇakuṭidāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 339), and the *Hāsajanakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 325) [DharmaNexus].
